questions.question: At the 2025 World Bank Land Conference, which country was honoured as a Country Champion in recognition of its transformative work in rural land governance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India** was honoured as a **Country Champion** at the **2025 World Bank Land Conference** for its transformative efforts in **rural land governance**. This recognition highlights India's significant progress in implementing land reforms and improving land administration systems.
 
• The award acknowledges India's use of **digital technologies** and innovative approaches to enhance **transparency, efficiency, and accessibility** in rural land records management.
 
• India's flagship program, **Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP)**, played a pivotal role in achieving this milestone. The program aims to digitize land records, reduce disputes, and ensure land ownership transparency.
 
• India has also focused on empowering rural communities by providing secure land tenure to marginalized groups, including women and tribal populations, under initiatives such as the **Forest Rights Act, 2006**.
 
• The recognition underscores India's commitment to achieving **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly Goal 1 (No Poverty) and Goal 15 (Life on Land), through effective rural land governance strategies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP):**

 
 
• Launched in **2008**, this program aims to digitize and modernize land records to enhance transparency and minimize land disputes.
 
• It focuses on integrating **spatial and non-spatial data**, providing a unified land information system accessible to stakeholders.
 
• DILRMP promotes the use of **GIS (Geographical Information System)** and **remote sensing technologies** for accurate land mapping.
 
 
 
• **Forest Rights Act, 2006:**
 
 
• This landmark legislation recognizes the rights of forest-dwelling communities over land and resources, ensuring their socio-economic empowerment.
 
• It aims to correct historical injustices faced by tribal populations and other traditional forest dwellers.
 
 
 
• **World Bank Land Conference:**
 
 
• An international platform where countries share best practices, policies, and innovations in land governance and administration.
 
• The conference focuses on achieving equitable land access and security to support sustainable development worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**
 
 
• Adopted by the United Nations in 2015, the SDGs aim to address global challenges like poverty, inequality, and environmental degradation by 2030.
 
• India's efforts in rural land governance contribute to achieving SDG Goal 1 (**No Poverty**) by reducing land disputes and ensuring secure land tenure.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India's Achievements in Rural Land Governance:**

 
 
• The use of **e-governance platforms** like the **Bhoomi Project** in Karnataka and **Bhulekh** in other states has streamlined land record management.
 
• India has effectively utilized satellite imagery and geospatial data for land surveys and mapping under programs like **SVAMITVA (Survey of Villages and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas)**.
 
• Special initiatives to address the needs of vulnerable groups, such as women and tribal populations, have contributed to inclusive land governance.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• According to the **World Bank's Ease of Doing Business Report**, land administration efficiency is crucial for fostering economic growth and investment.
 
• Countries around the world are adopting digital technologies to modernize land records and address issues like fraudulent transactions and land disputes.

questions.question: In May 2025, six African nations signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the World Health Organization (WHO) to combat Kala Azar. What does Kala Azar refer to?

options.text: A type of viral fever transmitted by mosquitoes
A bacterial infection spread through contaminated water
A parasitic disease caused by sandfly bites
A genetic disorder affecting red blood cells

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A parasitic disease caused by sandfly bites**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kala Azar, also known as visceral leishmaniasis**, is a parasitic disease caused by protozoa of the genus *Leishmania*, transmitted through bites of infected female sandflies (*Phlebotomus*).
 
• The disease affects the internal organs, particularly the liver, spleen, and bone marrow, and can be fatal if left untreated.
 
• Symptoms of Kala Azar include prolonged fever, weight loss, weakness, anemia, and swelling of the spleen and liver.
 
• Kala Azar is endemic in several African and Asian nations, including India, Bangladesh, Sudan, South Sudan, Ethiopia, and Kenya.
 
• The World Health Organization (WHO) considers it a neglected tropical disease and has prioritized its elimination in endemic countries through control programs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A type of viral fever transmitted by mosquitoes:**

 
 
• Diseases such as dengue fever, chikungunya, and Zika virus are examples of viral fevers transmitted by mosquitoes, particularly *Aedes aegypti*.
 
• Dengue fever is characterized by high fever, severe headache, muscle and joint pain, and skin rash.
 
• Unlike Kala Azar, these diseases are caused by viruses, not parasitic protozoa.
 
 
 
• **A bacterial infection spread through contaminated water:**
 
 
• Diseases such as cholera and typhoid are bacterial infections caused by consumption of water or food contaminated with the bacteria *Vibrio cholerae* and *Salmonella typhi*, respectively.
 
• Symptoms include severe diarrhea, dehydration, and fever, which differ significantly from Kala Azar's symptoms.
 
• Kala Azar is not spread through water; it is vector-borne and transmitted by sandflies.
 
 
 
• **A genetic disorder affecting red blood cells:**
 
 
• Genetic disorders such as sickle cell anemia and thalassemia affect the structure and function of red blood cells.
 
• Sickle cell anemia causes abnormally shaped red blood cells, leading to blockages in blood vessels and reduced oxygen delivery to tissues.
 
• These disorders are inherited and non-communicable, whereas Kala Azar is an infectious disease caused by parasites.
 
 
 
• **About Kala Azar:**
 
 
• Efforts to combat Kala Azar include early diagnosis, vector control measures (e.g., insecticide spraying), and effective treatment using antileishmanial drugs such as amphotericin B and miltefosine.
 
• WHO has set a target for eliminating Kala Azar as a public health problem in endemic regions by reducing cases to less than 1 per 10,000 population at the district level.

questions.question: On 20 June 2025, Prime Minister Narendra Modi officially flagged off India’s first indigenously manufactured locomotive export to which country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Republic of Guinea**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **20 June 2025**, Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** flagged off India's first **indigenously manufactured locomotive export**.
 
• The country receiving this export is the **Republic of Guinea**, a West African nation with growing trade relations with India.
 
• The locomotive was manufactured by **Indian Railways' Production Units**, showcasing India's capability to produce high-quality rail technology domestically.
 
• The initiative marks a significant milestone in India's "Make in India" campaign and its efforts to become a global exporter of advanced technology and infrastructure equipment.
 
• This export strengthens the **bilateral relationship** between India and the Republic of Guinea, contributing to the African nation's infrastructure development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indian Railways' Manufacturing Capabilities:**

 
 
• Indian Railways operates several **production units**, such as the **Chittaranjan Locomotive Works (CLW)**, Diesel Locomotive Works (DLW), and Modern Coach Factory (MCF).
 
• These units specialize in manufacturing **electric locomotives, diesel locomotives, and high-speed coaches** for domestic and international markets.
 
• India's locomotive exports highlight the country's ability to meet global quality standards and deliver cost-effective solutions.
 
 
 
• **Republic of Guinea:**
 
 
• The Republic of Guinea is located in **West Africa**, bordered by countries like Senegal, Mali, and Sierra Leone.
 
• It is rich in **bauxite reserves** and other natural resources, making it a significant trade partner for India.
 
• India has been fostering bilateral relations with Guinea through trade, developmental assistance, and capacity-building programs.
 
 
 
• **Make in India Campaign:**
 
 
• Launched in **2014** by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the "Make in India" initiative aims to make India a global manufacturing hub.
 
• The campaign focuses on enhancing infrastructure, streamlining processes, and encouraging foreign direct investment (FDI) in key sectors.
 
• The export of locomotives aligns with the campaign's goals, showcasing India's growing manufacturing and technological capabilities.
 
 
 
• **India-Africa Relations:**
 
 
• India is actively engaged in enhancing its partnership with African nations through initiatives such as the **India-Africa Forum Summit**.
 
• Key areas of cooperation include **infrastructure development, energy, health, and education**.
 
• The locomotive export is part of India's broader strategy to strengthen ties with Africa and contribute to its economic growth.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The locomotive export is a **first-of-its-kind initiative** for India, reinforcing its status as a global supplier of advanced rail technology.
 
• The Republic of Guinea is expected to utilize these locomotives for enhancing its **railway infrastructure**, boosting trade and connectivity within the region.
 
• India's expertise in manufacturing cost-effective and efficient rail solutions makes it a preferred partner for developing nations.
 
• The success of this export is likely to open up new opportunities for India's railway sector in other **global markets**, especially in Africa and Asia.

questions.question: What honour did ISRO chief V. Narayanan receive in Kolkata in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rammohan Mission Purashkar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rammohan Mission Purashkar** is a prestigious award given to individuals or organizations for their outstanding contributions in various fields, including science, technology, literature, and social service.
 
• In the year **2025**, **V. Narayanan**, the renowned chief of the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**, was honored with the Rammohan Mission Purashkar for his exceptional contributions to India's space research and technological advancements.
 
• **V. Narayanan** has played a pivotal role in strengthening ISRO’s capabilities, particularly in the areas of **cryogenic technology** and the development of advanced propulsion systems, which are critical for satellite launches and space exploration missions.
 
• This award highlights the efforts of Indian scientists in ensuring India’s global recognition in the field of **aerospace engineering** and **space exploration**.
 
• The award is named after **Raja Rammohan Roy**, a prominent social reformer of India, symbolizing the spirit of innovation and progress in the nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **V. Narayanan's Contributions to ISRO:**

 
 
• He is a distinguished scientist and the director of the **Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre (LPSC)**, a key facility of ISRO responsible for the design and development of liquid propulsion systems.
 
• Under his leadership, India successfully developed the **Cryogenic Upper Stage (CUS)** used in the GSLV Mk-II launch vehicle, marking a significant milestone in India's space program.
 
• He has been instrumental in advancing **semi-cryogenic propulsion technology**, which is critical for heavy-lift launch vehicles.
 
 
 
• **Rammohan Mission Purashkar:**
 
 
• This award is conferred annually to individuals who have made remarkable contributions to their respective fields, promoting the ideals of innovation and excellence.
 
• It aims to encourage and recognize efforts that contribute to the nation’s development and global standing.
 
 
 
• **ISRO’s Achievements in Recent Years:**
 
 
• ISRO has successfully launched several ambitious missions, including **Chandrayaan-2** and **Mangalyaan**, showcasing India’s capabilities in interplanetary exploration.
 
• The organization is currently working on the **Gaganyaan mission**, India’s first human spaceflight program, which is expected to be a landmark achievement.
 
• ISRO's launch vehicles, such as the **PSLV** and **GSLV**, have established India as a reliable player in the global satellite launch market.
 
 
 
• **Raja Rammohan Roy:**
 
 
• Known as the **Father of the Indian Renaissance**, Raja Rammohan Roy was a social reformer who played a key role in the abolition of practices like **Sati** and championed women's rights, education, and modern values.
 
• The award named after him symbolizes the fusion of traditional Indian values with modern scientific and technological advancements.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Prestigious Indian Awards:**

 
 
• **Bharat Ratna:** India’s highest civilian award, conferred for exceptional service in arts, literature, science, and public services.
 
• **Padma Awards:** Includes **Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan**, and **Padma Vibhushan**, given for contributions across various fields like arts, science, and social work.
 
• **National E-Governance Award:** Recognizes excellence in the implementation of e-Governance initiatives in the public sector.
 
 
 
• **India’s Space Ambitions:**
 
 
• India is striving to establish itself as a global leader in space exploration, with plans to develop **reusable launch vehicles**, **space stations**, and missions to the **Moon** and **Mars**.
 
• ISRO has been collaborating with other space agencies like **NASA**, **ESA**, and **Roscosmos** to share technologies and expertise.

questions.question: The 2025 World Kabaddi Cup was won by which of the following countries?

• The Indian Kabaddi team comprises highly skilled players who excel in both raiding and defending, making them a formidable force in global competitions.

• **Kabaddi:**

 
 
• **Kabaddi** is a contact team sport that originated in ancient India and is popular in South Asia.
 
• The game involves two teams competing to score points by raiding the opponent's territory and tagging players without being caught.
 
• Kabaddi is played in various formats, including **circle-style Kabaddi** and **standard-style Kabaddi**.
 
• The sport gained international recognition and was included in the **Asian Games**, further boosting its global popularity.
 
 
 
• **India's Achievements in Kabaddi:**
 
 
• India has won multiple **World Kabaddi Cups** and has been a consistent winner in the **Asian Games** since the sport was introduced.
 
• Indian players like **Anup Kumar**, **Pardeep Narwal**, and **Ajay Thakur** have become household names due to their exceptional performances.
 
• The **Pro Kabaddi League (PKL)**, launched in India, has further popularized the sport and brought international attention to Kabaddi.
 
 
 
• **Other Countries in Kabaddi:**
 
 
• **Iran:** Iran has emerged as a strong competitor in Kabaddi, winning medals in international tournaments such as the Asian Games.
 
• **South Korea:** South Korea has made significant progress in Kabaddi and is known for its strategic gameplay.
 
• **Pakistan:** Pakistan also participates in Kabaddi tournaments and has a strong presence in the sport, particularly in the circle-style format.
 
 
 
• **World Kabaddi Cup:**
 
 
• The **World Kabaddi Cup** is an international Kabaddi tournament organized periodically, featuring teams from various countries.
 
• It serves as a platform to showcase the talent and skills of Kabaddi players globally.
 
• The tournament includes both men's and women's categories, promoting gender equality in sports.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Pro Kabaddi League (PKL):** The PKL has played a crucial role in popularizing Kabaddi in India and internationally, attracting players from various countries.
 
• **Training Infrastructure:** India has well-established training centers and academies dedicated to Kabaddi, ensuring the development of world-class players.
 
• **Global Expansion:** Kabaddi's inclusion in international tournaments like the Asian Games and World Cup has contributed to its global reach and popularity.
 
• **Cultural Significance:** Kabaddi holds cultural importance in India, being a traditional sport that is deeply rooted in the country's heritage.

questions.question: What was the theme of the RBI’s Financial Literacy Week (FLW) 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Financial Literacy: Women’s Prosperity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **RBI’s Financial Literacy Week (FLW) 2025** was themed around **“Financial Literacy: Women’s Prosperity”**, highlighting the importance of empowering women through financial education.
 
• The primary objective of the theme was to promote **financial literacy among women**, enabling them to make informed financial decisions, manage resources efficiently, and achieve financial independence.
 
• The initiative emphasized the significance of educating women about **savings, investments, credit facilities**, and **digital financial tools** to enhance their participation in economic activities.
 
• Workshops, campaigns, and outreach programs were conducted across India to **raise awareness** about financial products and services tailored to women, such as microfinance and self-help groups.
 
• This theme aligns with the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly **Goal 5 (Gender Equality)** and **Goal 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth)**, by fostering women’s economic empowerment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Financial Literacy Week (FLW):**

 
 
• The **RBI** organizes **Financial Literacy Week** annually to promote awareness about key financial topics among citizens.
 
• Each year, the event focuses on a specific theme relevant to the **financial inclusion agenda** of the country.
 
• FLW aims to reach **rural and urban populations**, with special attention to underserved and vulnerable groups.
 
 
 
• **Women and Financial Inclusion:**
 
 
• As per the **Global Findex Database 2021**, women’s access to formal financial services in India has significantly improved, but a **gender gap** still exists.
 
• Empowering women financially leads to better household outcomes, as women tend to invest more in **education, health, and family welfare**.
 
 
 
• **Other Past Themes of FLW:**
 
 
• **2024:** “Digital Finance for All” – Promoting the adoption of digital payment systems and safe online transactions.
 
• **2023:** “Financial Inclusion: India’s Growth” – Focused on making financial services accessible to all sections of society.
 
 
 
• **Key Financial Schemes for Women in India:**
 
 
• **Mahila Samman Savings Certificate:** A government-backed savings scheme offering higher returns for women.
 
• **Stand-Up India Scheme:** Provides loans to women entrepreneurs, particularly in marginalized communities.
 
• **Self-Help Groups (SHGs):** Promote collective savings and credit access among rural women.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Microfinance:** Small loans provided to women in rural areas empower them to start businesses and improve their livelihoods.
 
• **Digital Financial Literacy:** Teaching women to use **UPI, mobile banking apps, and digital wallets** helps bridge the digital divide.
 
• **Government Collaboration:** The RBI partners with organizations like **NABARD** and **state-level agencies** to implement FLW initiatives effectively.
 
• **Financial Education Modules:** RBI provides simplified educational materials in regional languages to ensure better reach and understanding.

questions.question: Among India’s neighbours, which of the following countries have the better ranking than India in the Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) for 2024, released by Transparency International in February 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**China**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI)** is published annually by **Transparency International**, ranking countries based on perceived corruption levels in their public sector.
 
• In the **CPI for 2024**, released in **February 2025**, India ranked lower than **China**, signifying that China’s public sector is perceived as less corrupt than India’s.
 
• **China** has consistently scored higher than India in recent CPI rankings due to its stringent anti-corruption measures and reforms, including crackdowns on corrupt officials.
 
• The **CPI scores** are calculated using multiple data sources, including expert assessments and surveys conducted by independent institutions.
 
• Countries are ranked on a scale from **0 to 100**, where **0** indicates highly corrupt and **100** indicates very clean. China’s score is higher than India’s, indicating better performance in combating corruption.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI):**

 
 
• The CPI is a globally recognized metric that evaluates countries based on **corruption perception** in their public sector.
 
• It uses a combination of **expert surveys** and **business opinion polls** conducted by independent organizations.
 
• The CPI ranking provides insights into governance, transparency, and accountability in different nations.
 
• **Transparency International**, headquartered in Berlin, Germany, is the organization responsible for publishing the CPI.
 
 
 
• **China’s Anti-Corruption Efforts:**
 
 
• China has implemented several anti-corruption campaigns spearheaded by the Communist Party of China, targeting corrupt officials and practices.
 
• Notable initiatives include the **“Tigers and Flies” campaign**, focusing on corruption at both high-ranking and local levels.
 
• The establishment of agencies like the **National Supervisory Commission** strengthened oversight and enforcement mechanisms.
 
 
 
• **India’s Corruption Challenges:**
 
 
• India faces significant challenges in addressing corruption, including issues related to bureaucratic inefficiency, political interference, and lack of stringent enforcement of anti-corruption laws.
 
• Although initiatives like the **Lokpal Act** and digital governance reforms aim to combat corruption, implementation gaps remain.
 
• India’s CPI ranking is impacted by systemic issues such as **red tape**, lack of accountability, and opaque decision-making processes.
 
 
 
• **Other Neighboring Countries:**
 
 
• Countries like **Bangladesh, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka** have historically ranked lower than India in CPI due to higher perceived corruption levels.
 
• These countries often grapple with issues such as **weak governance**, lack of judicial independence, and political instability that exacerbate corruption.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Transparency International:**

 
 
• Founded in **1993**, Transparency International is a global non-governmental organization working to combat corruption.
 
• Its flagship **Corruption Perceptions Index** provides comprehensive data on corruption levels worldwide, influencing policy-making and governance reforms.
 
 
 
• **Global Trends in CPI:**
 
 
• Scandinavian countries like **Denmark**, **Finland**, and **Sweden** consistently rank among the least corrupt nations, scoring high in CPI rankings.
 
• Countries with strong institutions, transparent governance, and effective anti-corruption mechanisms generally perform better on the CPI scale.
 
 
 
• **India’s Initiatives Against Corruption:**
 
 
• India has introduced reforms like the **Right to Information (RTI) Act**, **Digital India campaign**, and **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** to reduce corruption.
 
• While these measures have improved transparency, challenges like enforcement and accountability persist.

questions.question: As per the Economic Survey, 2024–25, what is the global movement led by India to promote sustainable lifestyles called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**LiFE**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **LiFE** stands for **Lifestyle for Environment**, a global movement led by **India** to promote sustainable lifestyles.
 
• It was introduced by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** during the **2021 United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP26)** held in **Glasgow, Scotland**.
 
• The initiative emphasizes the importance of **mindful and deliberate utilization of resources**, moving away from mindless consumption.
 
• The concept of LiFE encourages people to adopt sustainable practices in their daily lives, such as reducing waste, conserving energy, and using environmentally friendly products.
 
• The **Economic Survey 2024–25** reiterates the importance of LiFE in combating **climate change** and achieving the goals of a **net-zero economy** by reducing carbon emissions through individual and collective actions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Origin of LiFE:**

 
 
• LiFE was conceptualized by India as part of its commitment to global environmental sustainability and was formally proposed by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** at COP26 in **November 2021**.
 
• The initiative aligns with the principles of the **Paris Agreement** to limit global warming to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of LiFE:**
 
 
• Encouraging individuals to adopt sustainable practices to reduce their carbon footprint.
 
• Promoting circular economy principles, such as **reuse, recycle, and repair**.
 
• Advocating for policies that support sustainable production and consumption patterns globally.
 
 
 
• **Global Impact of LiFE:**
 
 
• LiFE aims to create a **mass movement** for sustainable living by involving governments, businesses, and individuals worldwide.
 
• The movement emphasizes that climate action is not limited to governments and industries but also requires individual contributions.
 
• Countries and organizations worldwide have shown interest in collaborating with India on this initiative to tackle global environmental challenges.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of LiFE:**
 
 
• Focus on **behavioral change** to encourage environmentally conscious choices.
 
• Promotion of **eco-friendly technologies** and products.
 
• Integration of sustainability into **education systems** to raise awareness among younger generations.
 
 
 
• **India’s Role in Global Climate Action:**
 
 
• As a signatory to the **Paris Agreement**, India has committed to reducing its carbon intensity by 33-35% by 2030 (compared to 2005 levels).
 
• India is actively working towards achieving its **net-zero emissions target by 2070**.
 
• The LiFE movement complements India’s other initiatives, such as the **International Solar Alliance (ISA)** and the **National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Options Explained:**

 
 
• **Earth First:** A general term often used in environmental movements but not a specific initiative led by India.
 
• **Go Green:** A phrase promoting environmental consciousness but not related to the LiFE initiative.
 
• **Swachh Life:** This term might sound related to cleanliness drives like **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan**, but it is not the correct answer.
 
 
 
• **Key Achievements:**
 
 
• India’s efforts under LiFE have received international recognition for promoting **sustainable living**.
 
• The movement has inspired various global organizations to incorporate sustainability into their operations.
 
 
 
• **Link to Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**
 
 
• LiFE aligns with SDG 12 (**Responsible Consumption and Production**) and SDG 13 (**Climate Action**).
 
• It also contributes to SDG 7 (**Affordable and Clean Energy**) by promoting energy-efficient practices.

questions.question: In 2025, which company has partnered with the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) to restore heritage water bodies?

__
 
• **Bisleri**, a leading packaged drinking water company in India, has partnered with the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)** in 2025 to restore heritage water bodies across the country.
 
• The initiative is aimed at **reviving traditional water conservation systems** that were historically significant and played a key role in maintaining water availability.
 
• This partnership focuses on **restoration and rejuvenation of ancient stepwells, ponds, and other water bodies** situated at heritage sites under the protection of ASI.
 
• The collaboration aligns with the Indian government’s emphasis on **cultural preservation** and sustainable water resource management.
 
• Under this initiative, Bisleri has pledged to use its expertise and resources to ensure the **scientific and eco-friendly restoration** of these water bodies, while also raising awareness about their historical and environmental significance.

__
 
• **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI):**

 
 
• The ASI, under the Ministry of Culture, is responsible for the **protection and preservation of India’s cultural heritage**, including monuments, archaeological sites, and remains of national importance.
 
• It was established in **1861** by Alexander Cunningham and has since played a vital role in safeguarding India’s rich historical legacy.
 
• As of now, ASI protects and maintains over **3,600 monuments**, including ancient water structures.
 
 
 
• **Heritage Water Bodies:**
 
 
• These include traditional water storage systems such as **stepwells, kunds, baolis, and lakes**, which were constructed to meet water needs in historic times.
 
• Many of these structures, apart from serving as water sources, were architectural marvels and had **religious and cultural significance**.
 
• The restoration of these water bodies is crucial for addressing **water scarcity** issues and promoting heritage tourism.
 
 
 
• **About Bisleri:**
 
 
• Founded in **1969**, Bisleri is one of India’s most recognized brands in the **packaged drinking water industry**.
 
• The company is known for its focus on sustainability and has initiated various **CSR activities** related to water conservation.
 
• Its **‘Bottles for Change’ campaign** is a notable initiative aimed at recycling plastic waste and promoting environmental awareness.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives for Water Conservation:**
 
 
• Programs like **Jal Shakti Abhiyan** and **Atal Bhujal Yojana** have been launched to address water conservation and management issues in India.
 
• These programs focus on **rainwater harvesting**, rejuvenation of traditional water bodies, and groundwater recharge.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Restoration of heritage water bodies helps in **combating water scarcity** and promotes environmental sustainability.
 
• It also contributes to **heritage tourism**, creating awareness about India’s rich cultural and architectural legacy.
 
• Partnerships between private entities like Bisleri and public institutions like ASI exemplify the importance of **public-private collaboration** in addressing pressing environmental and heritage conservation challenges.
 
• The initiative aligns with global efforts toward achieving the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation) and SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities).
